*Brief bio:* Fred J. Hickernell is professor of applied mathematics. His
research focuses on improving the efficiency of computer simulations and
developing justifiable stopping criteria. He has spent most of his career at
Hong Kong Baptist University and Illinois Institute of Technology, often in
academic administrative roles. He has served on the editorial boards of the
Journal of Complexity, Mathematics of Computation, and the SIAM Journal on
Numerical Analysis. He is a Fellow of the Institute of Mathematical
Statistics and the recipient of the 2016 Joseph F. Traub Prize for Achievement
in Information-Based Complexity.

Hickernell speaks Cantonese and enjoys Chinese food. He is married with adult
children. He enjoys discussing matters of substance. His most important
identity is a disciple of Jesus.
